problem: Language-based navigation work (VLN, CVDN) assumes the agent's start location is already known, and localization from natural-language dialog in a realistic 3D building has no dataset or baseline. Prior dialog datasets are image-based or use abstract outdoor maps.
motivation: Localization is a precursor to navigation. Localizing a lost person from their verbal description, e.g. an emergency caller in a building, is a practical application. A cooperative setting with asymmetric information (a map-holding Locator and an embodied Observer) requires descriptive language, goal-driven questioning and active navigation.
key_idea: Introduce the Where Are You? (WAY) dataset of ~6k human Observer-Locator dialogs in Matterport3D and a LingUNet-Skip baseline that predicts the Observer's location as a pixel distribution on a top-down map conditioned on the dialog.
insight: The task is genuinely multimodal. Dialog-only (No Vision) gets 7.8% and map-only (No Dialog) 32.1% val-unseen Acc@3m, versus 45.6% for the full model, so unimodal priors are limited. Observer utterances matter more than Locator ones (44.9% vs 33.3%). Data augmentation is the largest modeling factor (-9.9% without it), and using only the first half of the dialog does as well as the full dialog (46.2%), showing the model fails to exploit late fine-grained turns.
method: Dialog encoder: the whole dialog is one token sequence with start/stop tokens around each message, encoded by a single-layer BiLSTM (300-d) with GloVe embeddings fine-tuned end-to-end.
Map encoder: the top-down floor render is scaled to 780x455 and passed through an ImageNet-pretrained frozen ResNet18 (truncated), giving a 98x57x128 feature map.

LingUNet-Skip: a 3-layer conv encoder-decoder in which 1x1 conv kernels predicted from the dialog modulate the features. Language-modulated skip connections are added, H_l = Deconv([H_{l+1}; G_l+F_l]). An MLP and softmax output a distribution over pixels.

Loss and inference: KL divergence to the ground-truth location smoothed by a 3m Gaussian. At inference the argmax pixel is used, and only the ground-truth final floor is processed for multi-floor buildings.
Data augmentation: color jitter, 180° rotation and 5% random cropping of the map.

Dataset collection: AMT pairs of Observer (first-person Matterport3D simulator, no map) and Locator (top-down floor maps). 2020 start locations across 87 buildings, 3 annotations each, giving 6,134 dialogs, with success defined at <3m error at the Observer's final position.
Baselines: Random, Random Node (oracle nav-graph nodes), Center, BLEU-retrieval plus SSIM patch matching (Heuristic), No Language, No Vision, and Human Locator.

setting.backbone: LingUNet-Skip with BiLSTM + GloVe and ResNet18 (ImageNet-pretrained, fixed); trained from scratch otherwise
setting.training_data: WAY train split: 3,967 dialogs from 58 Matterport3D environments; no extra data
setting.observation: top-down rendered floor map images (RGB) plus the text dialog; no Observer visual input
setting.action_space: none; predicts a single pixel location on the map (localization, not navigation)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (dataset collection via the Matterport3D simulator; model works on rendered top-down maps)
setting.privileged: The ground-truth final floor is used at inference; the full human dialog, including the Observer's actual navigation, is given as input

numbers_note: Human Locator reference: test LE 3.16, Acc@3m 70.4, Acc@5m 77.2. Center baseline on test: LE 6.71, Acc@3m 22.6.
results: LingUNet-Skip reaches 32.7% Acc@3m on unseen test buildings (45.6% on val-unseen, 53.5% on val-seen). This beats the strongest heuristic baseline, Center (22.6% test, 29.8% val-unseen), by 10 to 30 points absolute, but is far below human Locators at 70.4%. Its mean localization error is higher than Center's on val-unseen and test because of occasional large mistakes.
limitations: A large gap to humans remains (32.7% vs 70.4%), and the model does not exploit the second half of the dialog or handle long sequences well.
Only the LED task is modeled; the EVD and CL tasks are defined but have no baselines. The model uses only top-down maps, not panoramas or 3D, and inference uses the GT floor.
Dataset splits differ in difficulty (val-unseen is easier for humans), the dataset is small (~6k dialogs), and it includes failed human dialogs.
